title: Overviews on adverse events in pharmacological interventions
author: Elena Dorando
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bfgqjjvw
materials: included in SRs, data extraction methods, quality and risk of bias assessment s of individual studies (if presented/reported in the overview), quality and risk of bias assessments of systematic reviews, strategies to deal with discordant reviews, use of terminology, update strategies, strategies for dealing with overlapping reviews, grading of evi dence, synthesis methods, analysis (qualitative vs. quantitative), presentation of results (tabular, graphical, verbatim), causality assessments/considerations, publication bias, source(s) of funding , and conflicts/declaration of interest. In addition, we will collect the following content -related data: population, disease, (group) of drugs, route of administration, and all effect estimates of adverse events. These data will in particular inform the second objective. Quality assessment There is currently no tool to assess the methodological quality/risk of bias of overviews. However, w e will use the PRIO ( Preferred reporting items for overviews of systematic reviews) checklist 9 that was designed with a specific emphasis on harms in order to assess the reporting quality of the included overviews. Data synthesis For methodological and reporting characteristics, data will be analyzed descriptively. Data will be summarized as medians and interquartile ranges for continuous outcomes and as frequencies for categorical items. We will present data as extracted from the overviews without re -analyzing data from overviews, SRs or trials. The presentation of outcome data will be decided depending on the available data. We expect the presentation of outcome data to be very heterogeneous. However, preference will be given to tables over a narrative description. Where appropriate, we will consider converting effect estimates to facilitate the interpretation of the data. Further, we will present a map of the results to meet our second objective. Again, preference will be given to tables over a narrative descripti on. Furthermore, we will divide our results into the following categories: population, intervention, and (type of) adverse event. We will leave the possibility open for additional analyses depending on our included sample of overviews. We will create a c itation matrix to assess whether overlapping SRs exist (i.e. SRs that are included in more than one overview). To guide the interpretation, we will calculate the corrected covered area (CCA ) 17. In contrast to its original intent, the CCA will not be calculated at the overview level. Discussion Our review of overviews will provide a summary of all available evidence from overviews on adverse events in pha rmacological interventions. This data should serve as an easy -front end for decision makers. Our review will also be able to guide the methodological development of overviews on adverse events that have been a rather neglected area so far. We will mainly use passive dissemination strategies. steps.title: Perform Literature Search
steps.instruction: Search Medline (via OVID), EMBASE (via Elsevier), CDSR (via Cochrane Library), and Epistemonikos for published overviews in English, French, or German.

substeps.instruction: In Medline via OVID, use a validated search filter for overviews (ref 13) combined with a search filter for adverse events (ref 14).

Use the specific Medline search string: ((overview$ or review or synthesis or summary or Cochrane or analysis) and (reviews or meta-analyses or articles or umbrella)).ti. or "umbrella review".ab . or (meta -review or metareview).ti,ab. and ((ae OR co OR de).fs. OR (safe OR safety OR side effect* OR undesirable effect* OR treatment emergent OR tolerability OR toxicity OR adrs OR (adverse adj2 (effect OR effects OR reaction OR reactions OR event OR e vents OR outcome OR outcomes))).ti,ab.)
Adapt the search strategy for EMBASE.
Search CDSR using the term 'overview' in the title, abstract, and keywords.
Apply no restrictions on publication period.

steps.title: Manage Search Results
steps.instruction: Use Microsoft Excel to manage and analyze the results of the search.

steps.title: Screen Titles and Abstracts
steps.instruction: Screen retrieved titles and abstracts for eligibility.

substeps.instruction: One review author screens for eligibility.
A second reviewer evaluates titles/abstracts not considered relevant by the first (liberal acceleration).

steps.title: Conduct Full Text Screening
steps.instruction: Perform full text screening of eligible articles independently using two reviewers.

substeps.instruction: Resolve any discrepancies through discussion or by involving a third person.

steps.title: Prepare Data Extraction Form
steps.instruction: Test and refine the data extraction form before actual extraction.

substeps.instruction: Test the form using a set of 5 overviews.
Modify the form based on test feedback.

steps.title: Extract Data from Overviews
steps.instruction: Extract relevant methodological data from included overviews following the work of Pieper et al. (ref 16).

substeps.instruction: One reviewer extracts the data.
A second reviewer verifies the results.
Resolve discrepancies by consensus or by consulting a third person.

steps.title: Collect Specific Data Items
steps.instruction: Collect the following specific data points from each included overview:

substeps.instruction: Journal name and journal impact factor in the year of publication
Year of publication
Number of authors
Country of corresponding author
Registration (e.g., PROSPERO)
Protocol availability (as mentioned or referenced by authors)
Inclusion criteria
Primary outcomes
Number of databases searched
Search restrictions (language, date, publication status)
Selection methods
Number of included studies (SRs and primary studies)
Type of primary studies

Sometimes they are also called “umbrella review s”, “reviews of (systematic) reviews” or “meta -reviews”. Following Cochrane guidance, we henceforth refer to them as “overviews”.
